subtopic: KV cache capacity / Memory budget arithmetic
learningObjective: Compute the KV cache memory footprint of a specific model configuration and reason about capacity limits.
stem: Model configuration: 32 layers, H_kv = 8 KV heads, head_dim = 128, FP16 KV. The model weights occupy 26 GB on an 80 GB GPU. Which computation of KV cache capacity and its implication is correct?
profileData:
GPU: A100 80 GB (usable HBM ≈ 76 GB after runtime/allocator overhead)
Model weights (FP16): 26 GB
Activation + workspace budget: ~4 GB
Available for KV cache: ~46 GB
Model config: L=32 layers, H_kv=8, d=128, FP16 (2 bytes)
Per-token KV = 2 (K and V) * L * H_kv * d * 2 B = 2 * 32 * 8 * 128 * 2 = 131,072 B ≈ 128 KB

options.text: Per-token KV is ~256 KB; the cache holds ~180,000 tokens. If the average sequence length is 2000 tokens, that supports about 90 concurrent sequences before running out of KV cache.

Per-token KV is 8 * 128 * 2 = 2 KB (one KV entry across all layers). The cache holds ~23 million tokens. KV capacity is effectively unlimited for realistic workloads and cannot be a bottleneck on an 80 GB A100.

Per-token KV = 2 (K and V) * L * H_kv * d * 2 B = 128 KB. With 46 GB available for KV: 46 * 1024^3 / 131072 ≈ 376,832 tokens total. At 2000 tokens per sequence, that's ~188 concurrent sequences. Long-context (say 32K tokens/seq) drops this to ~11 concurrent sequences — a direct capacity constraint on batch size.

KV cache capacity is fixed by the model architecture alone (32 layers * 8 heads * 128 * 2 bytes = 65 KB) and does not scale with sequence length; capacity per GPU is therefore just ~700,000 sequences regardless of context length.

explanation: Per-token KV footprint (FP16, both K and V, across all layers) = 2 * L * H_kv * d * 2 B = 2 * 32 * 8 * 128 * 2 = 131,072 B (128 KB). With 46 GB available for KV, that supports 46 * 2^30 / 131072 ≈ 376,832 tokens in aggregate. If average sequence uses 2000 tokens of KV, the server can hold ~188 concurrent sequences. At 32K/sequence, only ~11 sequences fit — the direct reason long-context LLM serving has tiny effective batch sizes.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: 256 KB is double the correct value; likely double-counts the (K and V) factor or misuses H.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: forgets to multiply by number of layers and (K and V).
optionExplanations.C: Correct: standard KV cache arithmetic and its implication for batch size.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: KV cache scales linearly with tokens; the whole 'capacity' is per token per sequence position.

assumptions: FP16 KV storage (2 bytes per element).
L=32 layers, all with the same KV shape.
nonImplications: Does not imply the exact concurrent-sequence count matches production; batching efficiency and paging fragmentation eat some capacity.
Does not imply KV cache quantization is the only lever; MQA/GQA and shorter contexts also help.
